sections.heading: Section 1: Basic Antiderivatives & Power Rule for Integration

questions.answer: Apply the power rule: $\int 6x^2 dx = 2x^3$, $\int -4x dx = -2x^2$, $\int 7 dx = 7x$. Add constant of integration $C$.

questions.q: Find the general antiderivative of $f(x) = \sec^2 x + e^{3x}$.
questions.answer: $\int \sec^2 x dx = \tan x$ and $\int e^{3x} dx = \frac{1}{3}e^{3x} + C$.

sections.heading: Section 2: Left and Right Riemann Sums

questions.q: Approximate $\int_0^4 x^2 dx$ using a Left Riemann sum with $n = 4$ equal subintervals.
What is the Right Riemann sum approximation for the above integral with $n = 4$?
If $f(x)$ is strictly increasing on $[a, b]$, what is the relationship between Left and Right Riemann sums and the true integral value $I$?
questions.answer: For an increasing function, rectangles using left endpoints underestimate the area while right endpoints overestimate the area: $\text{Left} < I < \text{Right}$.

questions.q: Using the Trapezoidal Rule with $n = 4$ equal subintervals, approximate $\int_0^4 x^2 dx$.
If $f''(x) > 0$ (concave up) on $[a, b]$, how does the Trapezoidal Rule approximation compare to the exact integral?
choices: Trapezoidal Rule overestimates the true value
Trapezoidal Rule underestimates the true value
questions.answer: Chords connecting points on a concave up curve lie entirely above the curve, so trapezoids overestimate the true area.

questions.q: Approximate $\int_0^2 x^3 dx$ using a Midpoint Riemann sum with $n = 2$ equal subintervals.

sections.heading: Section 4: Limit of a Riemann Sum & Definite Integrals

questions.q: Which definite integral is equal to $\lim_{n \to \infty} \sum_{i=1}^n (1 + \frac{2i}{n})^3 \frac{2}{n}$?
questions.answer: Here $\Delta x = \frac{2}{n}$, interval length $= 2$. $x_i = 1 + i \Delta x \Rightarrow a = 1, b = 3$. The function is $f(x) = x^3$, giving $\int_1^3 x^3 dx$.

questions.q: Express $\int_0^5 \sqrt{x} dx$ as a limit of a Right Riemann sum.
questions.answer: $\Delta x = \frac{5}{n}$ and right endpoints are $x_i = \frac{5i}{n}$, so the sum is $\lim_{n \to \infty} \sum_{i=1}^n \sqrt{\frac{5i}{n}} \frac{5}{n}$.
